sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Washington County, KY?
sections.html:
Three offices in Springfield share the work. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets the assessed value of each parcel, the Sheriff's Office collects the bill from October through April 15, and the County Clerk takes over any bill that is still open after that date. The PVA does not set the rate and does not take payments.

The county's own tax page lists these numbers: PVA at 859-336-5420 for acreage, assessment, or a wrong name or mailing address on a bill; Sheriff at 859-336-5400 for payment questions or a bill that never arrived; County Clerk at 859-336-5425 for a payoff on any prior-year delinquency. Payments go to the Sheriff's property tax page address, 124 East Main Street, Springfield, KY 40069.

Real estate bills are addressed to the owner of record as of January 1, or to the current owner according to PVA records. If you bought or sold during the year and a bill reaches the wrong person, tell the PVA or the Sheriff early so it can be redirected.

sections.h2: When are Washington County tax bills due, and what is the discount?
sections.html:
Bills are due by December 31 of the assessment year, and a 2 percent discount applies to full payment made by November 1. The Sheriff normally receives the bills from the County Clerk between the first and the middle of October, and by statute cannot accept payment before then. Most owners can expect the bill by about October 15, and the printed bill carries four due dates with a dollar amount beside each.

Washington County payment windows under KRS 134.015
Payment madeAmount owed
By November 1Bill less 2 percent
November 2 to December 31Face amount
January 1 to January 31Face amount plus 5 percent
February 1 to April 15Face amount plus 10 percent

If the state delays the mailing, the Department of Revenue can switch to an alternative schedule measured in months from the mailing date. After April 15 the unpaid bill leaves the Sheriff's Office entirely.

sections.h2: How do I pay a Washington County property tax bill?
sections.html:
The Sheriff accepts only a few forms of payment, and the office has said why: card fees would be passed on to taxpayers, so it takes none. Plan around these rules.

  • Pay by check, money order, or cash. Cash works only in person. Make checks payable to the Washington County Sheriff's Office.
  • Mail the payment with the yellow postcard from the bill, even if you are sending several bills in one envelope, so each is credited to the right parcel.
  • Drop it in the box outside the office after hours, or hand it over during business hours and receive a receipt on the spot. Mail-in payers who want a receipt enclose a stamped, self-addressed envelope.
  • A payment postmarked on or before a due date is treated as received that day.
  • Partial payments are mailed back. There is no online payment option.

That last rule matters for sellers: a payoff for part of a year will not clear the account, so the full bill amount has to be paid or settled through the closing.

sections.h2: How is a Washington County assessment set and challenged?
sections.html:
Kentucky values property as it stands on January 1. A purchase price recorded in a deed may be used as the listed value for the following January 1 when the property has not changed. The tax roll is then opened to public view for 13 days starting the first Monday in May, six days a week including Saturday.

Disagreeing with the number follows a fixed order, set out by the Department of Revenue:

  • Confer with the PVA or a deputy first. They must explain how the value was reached and keep a written record of the meeting.
  • File the appeal with the County Clerk by the close of business on the day after the inspection period ends.
  • The local board of assessment appeals sits 25 to 35 days after inspection closes, for up to five days.
  • Bring evidence such as land and building descriptions, insurance policies, construction cost, and sales listings. A filing without documents is denied.

An owner who files and then skips the hearing cannot carry the dispute on to the Kentucky Claims Commission. Anyone paid to represent an owner must fall in a listed class, such as an attorney, CPA, or licensed appraiser, and carry written authorization. If the final value ends up above the figure you claimed and bills have already gone out, the clerk issues a supplemental bill for the difference.

sections.h2: What can lower a Washington County homeowner's bill?
sections.html:
The homestead exemption is the main tool. Owners aged 65 or older, and owners classified as totally disabled, can deduct $49,100 from the assessed value of the home they live in for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. The county's tax page describes the disability track as open to owners who are 100 percent disabled, and asks for the Social Security award letter at the PVA office.

Here is what that looks like at the Census median value for Washington County owner-occupied homes, $179,200. The taxable base drops to $130,100. The state's 2025 real property rate, 10.6 cents per $100 (down from 10.9 cents in 2024), would then produce about $137.91 instead of $189.95 for the state share. County, school, and district rates are extra, so ask the PVA for the full combined rate on a given parcel.

Apply at the PVA, not the Sheriff. Age can be shown with a birth certificate, driver's license, or passport. Once granted, an age-based exemption stays in place while you own and live in the home, so a seller should tell the PVA after closing.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid taxes when I sell a Washington County house?
sections.html:
The tax is the owner's personal debt from the assessment date, and the lien that attaches when it goes delinquent follows the land for 11 years, whoever owns it (KRS 134.015 and 134.420). A title company will find it. Ask the Sheriff what has been paid on the parcel before you list, and ask the Clerk for a payoff on any earlier year.

On April 15 the open bill moves to the County Clerk as a certificate of delinquency, with a 10 percent penalty and a sheriff's add-on fee, and interest of 1 percent per month starts. The county attorney mails notices, and the clerk may hold a tax sale between 90 and 135 days after the transfer, at which point a third-party buyer can take over the lien and add its own fees. Clearing the account before April 15 avoids all of that.

Property taxes in Washington County are normally prorated at closing: the seller pays for the part of the year they owned the home, and the buyer pays the whole bill when it arrives. The settlement statement prepared by the closing attorney or bank shows what was agreed.

sections.h2: What is Washington County, Kentucky like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Washington County was created in 1792 from part of Nelson County and was the first county formed after Kentucky became a state. Springfield is the seat, with Mackville and Willisburg as the other two cities. The courthouse, finished in 1816, is the oldest one still in use in Kentucky. About 297 square miles of land are home to roughly 12,368 people, a gain of 2.8 percent since the 2020 count.

Washington County Schools serves the county, with campuses in Springfield and Willisburg. Neighbors are Anderson, Mercer, Boyle, Marion, and Nelson counties, and the county sits on Eastern time. Census QuickFacts gives this picture of the housing stock:

  • 5,325 housing units and 4,852 households.
  • 77.6 percent of homes are lived in by their owners.
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $179,200.
  • Median household income: $61,616, with 14.1 percent of residents in poverty.
  • Workers travel 22.4 minutes to work on average.

Only 26 building permits were recorded in 2025, so most buyers are looking at houses that already stand. A seller with an older farmhouse, a property that needs repairs, or a bill that has slipped to the Clerk can sell the house as-is and settle the tax at the same closing.

faqs.q: When do Washington County property tax bills go out?
faqs.a: Bills reach the Sheriff's Office between early and mid October, and most owners get theirs by about October 15. The Sheriff cannot take payment before the bills arrive.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Washington County tax bill with a credit card?
faqs.a: No. The Sheriff takes check, money order, or cash in person, and offers no online payment. Debit and credit cards are not accepted because the fees would fall on taxpayers.

faqs.q: Where do I pay delinquent Washington County taxes from a prior year?
faqs.a: Pay the County Clerk at 859-336-5425, who gives the payoff amount. Bills still unpaid after April 15 are turned over to the Clerk with added penalties and interest.

faqs.q: Who pays the property tax when a Washington County house sells mid-year?
faqs.a: It depends on the contract, but the seller usually pays a pro-rated share at closing for the months they owned the home. The buyer is then billed for the full year. Check the settlement statement.

faqs.q: Does a Washington County homeowner over 65 get a tax break?
faqs.a: Yes. The homestead exemption deducts $49,100 from the assessed value for 2025 and 2026. File the application with the PVA at 859-336-5420 and bring proof of age.
